root: repo - Tool-neutral build entry with two implementations: Nx with Bun (default) and Bazel.
Usage:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel|semio] <command> [options] [-- <arguments>]
repo <command> --help [--lang=en|de]
Commands:
run <project:target[:configuration]>            Run one task of one project.
run-many --targets=<targets> [--projects=<projects>]
Run the same targets in many projects.
affected --targets=<targets>                    Run targets in the projects changed against HEAD and their dependents.
exec --projects=<projects> -- <command>         Run a command once per selected project, in the project root.
watch --projects=<projects> -- <command>        Rerun a command when selected source files change.
graph                                           Print the tool-neutral build graph.
show projects|project <name>|targets            Print projects, one project or all targets of the neutral graph.
inputs <project:target[:configuration]>         Print what the selected implementation hashes for one task: files, environment, runtime values and external packages.
reset                                           Invalidate the graph and reset the selected tool's local state.
tools setup [nx|bazel|semio|toolchains|all]|verify [tool...]|list [--json]|exec <tool|command> -- <arguments>
Provision the pinned tools for this host, report where it differs from the pins and run every other external tool through the tool registry.
preflight                                       Check the host against the finite requirements before any store is provisioned.
incremental list|plan|prepare|run|discard       Prove in a disposable copy that Nx and Bazel rebuild exactly what an edit affects, no more and no less.

concurrency list|plan|run                       Prove that simulated agents working in one checkout copy at the same time never wait for unrelated projects, share cached work and get the results of a serial run, with Nx and Bazel.

conformance list|plan|run                       Judge every build backend against the same language-agnostic scenarios: plan, run, cache hit and miss, outputs, test results, affected, cancellation, progress, concurrency and remote cache.

units plan|run|emit|exec                        Plan, run and emit language-neutral compilation units (Go, Python, .NET, C/C++, WIT, TeX) whose dependents re-run only when a dependency's interface changes, and execute one unit as the action of Nx or Bazel.

bench list|run|compare|acceptance               Measure the performance objectives (hot-cache latency, edit to rebuild per language, cache hit rate, graph, memory, concurrent agents) in a disposable checkout copy, judge them against the SLO table and compare with a stored baseline; `bench acceptance` holds the acceptance scenarios of the three products (hot no-op, peer edit, one-line edit with byte-exact revert) on the checkout itself to declared budgets.
dependencies sync|lock --all|--scope <owner> | ensure
Install, lock or ensure the workspace dependencies.
cargo --store=shared|isolated --configuration=prototype|release [--parallelism=<cores>] -- <cargo subcommand> <args>
Compile through the repository's Cargo ingress gate.
cache status|gc|verify|dedupe|clear             Show and collect every declared cache home with its budget, or clear the selected tool's local task cache.
remote-cache serve|status|gc                    Serve a bounded, shared result cache for Bazel and Nx from this machine, inspect the remote cache contract and the server, or collect the cache store.
capacity status|run                             Show the machine's free memory, floor, load and the running and waiting grants, or run any command under a machine-wide capacity grant.

leases status                                   Show which processes hold and wait for resource leases, how long, who blocks whom, deadlock cycles, lock order violations and the machine's admission queue.

fleet status                                    Show one picture of the shared workspace: who runs what (phase, progress, age, priority, code freshness), the queues with waiting-time estimates, memory admitted against really used, the Bazel servers, storage against its budgets, the sealed implementation and the last graph generation.
service status|start|stop|restart|issue|revoke|drop-caches|probe
Run, inspect or stop the resident service of this worktree that keeps the graph, file digests and task results warm and answers every agent over one local socket.
remote-execution serve|status|workers           Run the in-house remote execution service that hermetic Bazel actions can run on, inspect it, or join this machine to it as a worker.
doctor [--json] [--fix [--dry-run]] [--only=<area>[,<area>]] [--strict] [--facts]

Answer in one shot why work is waiting, slow or failing: tool pins, storage images, leases, capacity grants, agent sessions, graph and dependency generations, caches, running repo processes and the host, each problem with its owner and the command that resolves it.

session open|status|close|list                  Show, open and close agent sessions: one identity per agent working in this worktree, with its cargo lane, Bazel slot preference, Nx daemon namespace, test sandbox root, lease owner tag, budget share and capability.
Options:
--foreground                                    service start: run the service in this terminal instead of detached. (used by: service)
--agent=<id>                                    service issue: the agent the token is issued to; service revoke: revoke every session of this agent. (used by: service, session)
--classes=<classes>                             service issue: comma separated command classes the token allows (status, query, run, watch, admin). (used by: service)
--for=<names>                                   service issue: comma separated project names or prefixes ending in * the token is limited to. (used by: service)
--ttl=<seconds>                                 service issue: lifetime of the token in seconds (default 3600, at most 86400). (used by: service)
-p, --projects=<projects>                       Comma list of project names with * wildcards, tag:<tag>, name:<name>, directory:<root> and !<pattern> negation. (used by: run-many, exec, watch)
--exclude=<projects>                            Comma list of projects to leave out (same patterns as --projects). (used by: run-many, affected, exec, watch)
-t, --targets=<targets>, --target               Comma list of target names or * patterns. (used by: run-many, affected)

-c, --configuration=<prototype|release>         Compiler configuration; disagreeing values (also a :<configuration> suffix or SEMIO_BUILD_MODE) are refused; cargo takes the full name only. (used by: run, run-many, affected, cargo)
--parallel=<n>                                  Maximum number of concurrent tasks. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--bail                                          Stop at the first failing task. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--verbose                                       Print more detail. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--output=<stream|stream-without-prefixes|static>, --output-style
Output style of the task logs. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--skip-cache                                    Ignore the task cache. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--skip-remote-cache                             Ignore the remote cache. (used by: run, run-many, affected)
--exclude-dependencies, --exclude-task-dependencies
Run only the named tasks, not the tasks they depend on. (used by: run, run-many, affected)

--dry-run                                       Print the task graph as a DryRunPlan on stdout and execute nothing; the same for every tool. With cache gc or remote-cache gc: list what would be removed and remove nothing. (used by: run, run-many, affected, exec, cache, remote-cache, doctor)

--graph[=<file>]                                Same as --dry-run; with a file the plan is written there (Nx: the file as given, Bazel: a report whose path is printed). (used by: run, run-many, affected, exec)

--all                                           Select every project (affected, watch), every dependency owner (dependencies) or every lease directory with registered processes (leases). (used by: affected, watch, dependencies, leases, session)
--base=<ref>                                    Compare against this revision instead of HEAD. (used by: affected)
--head=<ref>                                    End revision of the comparison. (used by: affected)
--files=<files>                                 Comma list of changed files instead of the git comparison. (used by: affected)
--uncommitted                                   Only uncommitted changes. (used by: affected)
--untracked                                     Only untracked files. (used by: affected)
--include-global-files                          Also react to files outside any project. (used by: watch)
--file=<path>                                   Write the result as a report file and print its path. (used by: graph, show, incremental, concurrency, bench, conformance, units)

--json                                          Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line. (used by: graph, show, incremental, concurrency, bench, capacity, fleet, leases, cache, remote-cache, doctor, tools, conformance, units, service, session)

--area=<id[,id]>                                cache status|gc: limit the report or the collection to these ledger areas (or retired, undeclared); cache dedupe: limit the search to these places (bazel-outputs, bazel-workspaces, vite-products, tools). (used by: cache)

--budget=<size>                                 cache status|gc: the disk budget of this machine for this call (an integer or a number with KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, e.g. 40GiB); it beats the SEMIO_CACHE_BUDGET_BYTES variable, which beats the machine file in the repository cache root, which beats the declared default. (used by: cache)

--deep                                          cache verify (required): read every indexed optional graph leaf and every closure inventory again and compare it with its recorded hash. cache status: walk every cache home now (with progress, cancellable) and record the sizes, instead of reading statfs and the size ledger. (used by: cache)
--tasks                                         cache status: print the selected tool's task cache (a CacheStatus) instead of the cache ledger. (used by: cache)

--graph-policy=<fresh|current>                  fresh (default) verifies the graph and waits for a rebuild when a project changed; current serves the newest sealed graph at once and never waits; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_GRAPH_POLICY. (used by: graph, show)

--scenario=<ids|all>                            incremental plan|run and bench acceptance: comma list of scenario ids, or all (bench acceptance also takes kind:<noop|peer|edit> and product:<course|print|dashboard>; without --in-place, all leaves the scenarios that edit files out). (used by: incremental, conformance, bench)

--implementations=<nx|bazel|semio>              incremental and concurrency plan|run: implementations to judge (default: every registered backend). (used by: incremental, concurrency, bench, conformance)

--root=<path>                                   incremental, concurrency, bench: the disposable repository copy (default: the folder .sinc in the home directory, else sinc in the temporary directory of the process, else /tmp/sinc); it must not lie inside or contain the checkout, and its path stays short because absolute paths are limited to 256 characters. (used by: incremental, concurrency, bench, units)
--phases=<warm,edit,revert>                     incremental run: phases to judge (default: all three). (used by: incremental)
--fresh                                         incremental prepare: discard the copy and clone it again. (used by: incremental)
--workloads=<ids|all>                           concurrency plan|run: comma list of workload ids, or all. (used by: concurrency)
--sessions=<n>                                  concurrency plan|run: simulated agents per workload, the first n of its sessions (default: 3, at most 8). (used by: concurrency)
--criteria=<id>                                 concurrency run: judge every workload with this set of pass criteria instead of its own. (used by: concurrency)
--keep                                          conformance run: keep the scratch workspaces for inspection. (used by: conformance)
--slo=<ids|all>                                 bench run: comma list of objective ids, probe:<id>, kind:<cli-help|noop|edit|graph|cache|concurrency>, or all. (used by: bench)

--runs=<n>                                      bench run: samples per probe instead of the authored count (the 95th percentile needs 20 samples, the 99th needs 100; fewer leave those objectives unproven). (used by: bench)
--baseline=<path>                               bench run|compare: a stored report to compare with; a change beyond the tolerance of an objective is a regression or an improvement. (used by: bench)
--save-baseline=<path>                          bench run: store the report as the baseline of later runs. (used by: bench)

--history=<folder>                              bench run: store the report in this folder as <UTC start>-<host class>.json and compare with the newest earlier report of this host class when no --baseline is given; bench compare: compare the two newest reports of this host class. (used by: bench)
--current=<path>                                bench compare: the stored report to judge against --baseline. (used by: bench)
--markdown=<path>                               bench run|compare|acceptance: also write the report as a markdown file. (used by: bench)
--max-load=<per-core>                           bench run: refuse to start when the one-minute load per core of the host exceeds this number. (used by: bench)
--prepare                                       bench run: discard and prepare the disposable copy first, so that the cold graph probe starts from a copy without graph. (used by: bench)

--in-place                                      bench acceptance: run the scenarios that edit and restore source files in this checkout (a CI runner, a private clone); nobody else may edit it meanwhile. (used by: bench)
--scope <owner>                                 Restrict the operation to one dependency owner. (used by: dependencies)
--store=<shared|isolated>                       Cargo target store; never create a private target directory. (used by: cargo)
--parallelism=<cores>                           Positive number of cores for Cargo. (used by: cargo)
--port <port>                                   remote-cache serve: port to listen on; 0 picks a free port (default from the build policy). (used by: remote-cache)
--host <address>                                remote-cache serve: address to listen on; beyond loopback a token is required. (used by: remote-cache)

--directory <path>                              remote-cache serve|status|gc: store directory, relative to the workspace root (default: the remote cache home of the cache ledger). (used by: remote-cache)
--max-bytes <bytes>                             remote-cache serve|gc: upper bound of the store; the least recently used entries are evicted beyond it. (used by: remote-cache)
--read-only                                     remote-cache serve: refuse every write with 403, whatever token is presented. (used by: remote-cache)

--tls-certificate <path>                        remote-cache serve, remote-execution serve: PEM certificate chain; together with --tls-key the server speaks HTTPS (grpcs for the execution service). (used by: remote-cache, remote-execution)
--tls-key <path>                                remote-cache serve, remote-execution serve: PEM private key of the certificate. (used by: remote-cache, remote-execution)

--bind <address>                                remote-execution serve: address both listeners bind to (default 127.0.0.1); beyond loopback the cache tokens and the worker token are required. (used by: remote-execution)
--grpc-port <port>                              remote-execution serve: port of the gRPC listener for build tools (default 8980); 0 picks a free port. (used by: remote-execution)
--worker-port <port>                            remote-execution serve: port of the HTTP listener for workers and status (default 8981); 0 picks a free port. (used by: remote-execution)

--cache <url>                                   remote-execution serve: the shared store to use, the URL of a running repo remote-cache server; by default serve starts the store itself. (used by: remote-execution)
--local-workers <n>                             remote-execution serve: worker processes started with the service (default 1; 0 starts none). (used by: remote-execution)
--concurrency <n>                               remote-execution serve|workers: actions one worker runs at the same time (default: one per CPU). (used by: remote-execution)

--advertise <host>                              remote-execution serve: the host name clients and workers use to reach the service (default: loopback, else this machine's name). (used by: remote-execution)
--sandbox <auto|darwin-sandbox|linux-sandbox|isolated-root>
remote-execution serve|workers: how workers confine an action (default: the first available strategy of the hermetic table for this host). (used by: remote-execution)

--work-directory <path>                         remote-execution serve|workers: directory of a worker's blob cache and private input roots, relative to the workspace root (default: the remote execution home of the cache ledger). (used by: remote-execution)

--join <url>                                    remote-execution workers|status: the worker API of the scheduler, for example http://build-host:8981 (default: SEMIO_REMOTE_EXECUTION_SCHEDULER). (used by: remote-execution)
--name <name>                                   remote-execution workers: name of the worker in status and logs (default: host name and process id). (used by: remote-execution)
--properties <name=value,...>                   remote-execution workers: platform properties the worker offers in addition to OSFamily and Arch. (used by: remote-execution)
--operation=<name>                              capacity run: the catalogue operation whose estimate is reserved (default: command). (used by: capacity)
--memory=<megabytes>                            capacity run: reserve exactly this many megabytes instead of an operation's estimate. (used by: capacity)
--cpu=<cores>                                   capacity run: cores the command keeps busy, counted against the load ceiling (default: 1). (used by: capacity)
--jobs=<n>                                      capacity run: jobs of a task operation to reserve (default: 1). (used by: capacity)
--cwd=<path>                                    tools exec: the directory the tool runs in (default: the current directory). (used by: tools)
--light                                         tools exec: run without waiting for machine capacity, for short queries. (used by: tools)
--lease-directory=<path>                        leases status: the lease directory to inspect (default: the checkout's lease store). (used by: leases)
--limit=<n>                                     fleet status: how many runs the text output lists (default: 20, the JSON output always lists all). (used by: fleet)
--violations=<n>                                leases status: how many recent lock order violations to list (default: 10). (used by: leases)

--fix                                           doctor: apply the declared safe repairs for the findings (publications of dead processes, stale lease registry rows, gone agent sessions); with --dry-run list what they would remove. (used by: doctor)
--only=<area[,area]>                            doctor: limit the report to these areas (tools, storage, leases, capacity, sessions, graph, dependencies, caches, processes, host). (used by: doctor)
--strict                                        doctor: exit with status 1 for warnings as well as errors. (used by: doctor)
--facts                                         doctor: print the raw facts document the findings are derived from, as JSON, instead of the report. (used by: doctor)

--for=<go|python|dotnet|cpp|wit|tex>            units plan|run|emit: the source language whose units are planned (go, python, dotnet, cpp through CMake and Ninja, wit, tex; the tracked files of the checkout). (used by: units)
--out=<path>                                    units emit: the directory that receives the spec files and the build files; units exec: the result file of the unit (out.json). (used by: units)

--out-root=<path>                               units exec: read the files of the dependencies from and write the files of the unit below this directory (the layout the Nx targets use) instead of naming each file. (used by: units)
--spec=<path>                                   units exec: the spec file of the unit to execute. (used by: units)
--iface=<path>                                  units exec: the interface file (iface.json) the unit publishes. (used by: units)
--iface-dep=<path>                              units exec: the interface file of one dependency whose interface the unit consumes; repeatable. (used by: units)
--impl-dep=<path>                               units exec: a result file (out.json) of the implementation closure of the unit; repeatable. (used by: units)
--only=<unit-id>                                units run: run only this unit and its dependencies; repeatable. (used by: units)
--concurrency=<n>                               units run: units executed at the same time, 1 to 16 (default: 1). (used by: units)
--receipts=<path>                               units run: directory of the shared receipts, so later runs and other sessions reuse results (default: memory only). (used by: units)
--client=<name>                                 session open: the name of the agent client, used to name the agent of an MCP connection when no client variable identifies it. (used by: session)
--client-pid=<pid>                              session open: the process id of the agent client of a connection (part of the connection's identity). (used by: session)
--owner-pid=<pid>                               session open: a process whose end ends the session (default: the nearest agent-client ancestor). (used by: session)
--weight=<n>                                    session open: the weight of the session in the budget split between live sessions, 1 to 16 (default: 1). (used by: session)
--export                                        session open: also print the environment line NAME=value that attaches child processes to the session. (used by: session)
--dead                                          session close: close every gone session instead of one. (used by: session)
--force                                         session close: close a session although its owner process is still alive. (used by: session)
Global options:
--tool=<nx|bazel|semio>       Select the build implementation; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, then the policy default (nx).
--workers=<on|off>            Run actions in persistent workers (on) or in one process each (off); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, then the worker policy of the build policy.
--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo run @semio-tech/semio-tech-play:serve
Run the serve task with the default implementation.
repo run-many --targets=test --projects=tag:rust
Run the test target in every project tagged rust.
repo affected --targets=test
Test what changed against HEAD plus untracked files.
repo exec --projects=@semio-tech/repo-client -- repo tools exec bun -- test
Run one command inside one project root.
repo watch --projects=@semio-tech/repo-client -- repo run @semio-tech/repo-client:build
Rebuild one project on every source change.
repo graph --file=graph.json
Write the graph as a report file.
repo show projects
List all projects.
repo --tool=nx inputs @teaching/architecture-course:test
List the inputs Nx hashes for the course tests.
repo reset --tool=bazel
Reset the Bazel state.
repo tools setup all
Provision Nx, Bazel and every native toolchain at its pin.
repo preflight
Check architecture, free space, tools and directory exchange.
repo incremental list
List the incremental build scenarios.
repo concurrency list
List the concurrent workloads.
repo conformance list
List the conformance scenarios.
repo units plan --for=go
Plan the Go units of the checkout.
repo bench list
List the performance objectives.
repo dependencies lock --all
Regenerate the lock after editing a package.json.
repo cargo --store=shared --configuration=prototype -- check -p <crate> --lib
Type-check one crate in the shared store.
repo cache status
Show every cache partition and area against its budget.
repo remote-cache serve
Serve a local remote cache on 127.0.0.1:6090.
repo capacity status
See how much memory the machine has left above its floor and who holds it.
repo leases status
See who holds the repository's leases, who waits behind whom and for how long.
repo fleet status
See at a glance who runs what, who waits for what and for how long, and what the disk and memory budgets look like.
repo service start
Keep this worktree's graph and results warm for every agent.
repo remote-execution serve
Run the service on 127.0.0.1:8980 with the shared store and one local worker; hermetic Bazel actions can then run remotely.
repo doctor
See who waits for whom, what is slow and what is broken, with the command that fixes each finding.
repo session status
See which agent session this command belongs to and what it holds.
run: repo run - Run one task of one project.
Usage:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel|semio] run <project:target[:configuration]> [options]
Options:
-c, --configuration=<prototype|release>         Compiler configuration; disagreeing values (also a :<configuration> suffix or SEMIO_BUILD_MODE) are refused; cargo takes the full name only.
--parallel=<n>                                  Maximum number of concurrent tasks.
--bail                                          Stop at the first failing task.
--verbose                                       Print more detail.
--output=<stream|stream-without-prefixes|static>, --output-style
Output style of the task logs.
--skip-cache                                    Ignore the task cache.
--skip-remote-cache                             Ignore the remote cache.
--exclude-dependencies, --exclude-task-dependencies
Run only the named tasks, not the tasks they depend on.

--dry-run                                       Print the task graph as a DryRunPlan on stdout and execute nothing; the same for every tool. With cache gc or remote-cache gc: list what would be removed and remove nothing.
--graph[=<file>]                                Same as --dry-run; with a file the plan is written there (Nx: the file as given, Bazel: a report whose path is printed).
Global options:
--tool=<nx|bazel|semio>       Select the build implementation; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, then the policy default (nx).
--workers=<on|off>            Run actions in persistent workers (on) or in one process each (off); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, then the worker policy of the build policy.
--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo run @semio-tech/semio-tech-play:serve
Run the serve task with the default implementation.
repo run @semio-tech/semio-tech-play:serve --tool=bazel
Run the same task with Bazel.
repo run @semio-tech/semio-tech-play:serve --dry-run
Print the task graph and run nothing.
Notes:
- --dry-run prints a DryRunPlan on stdout and executes nothing; --graph is the same flag for every tool and takes an optional file.

- Bazel: a selection builds exactly the transitive closure of its tasks in one generated workspace; a cached test-family task without declared outputs and without dependents runs as a Bazel test (cached test results; only tests are built when only tests are selected; --skip-cache switches the cached test results off), every other task as a cacheable build action. Test sharding is not offered because the neutral contract defines no shard protocol.

repo tools setup all
Provision Nx, Bazel and every native toolchain at its pin.
repo tools verify
Report every pinned tool that is missing or differs from its pin.
repo tools list
See which external tools exist, how they are pinned and where this host has them.
repo tools exec cargo -- check -p semio-framework-value
Run Cargo through the registry instead of calling it directly.
repo tools exec --light rustc -- -vV
Ask an executable that a registered tool owns (rustc belongs to Cargo) for its version.
repo tools exec uv -- run python3 <script>.py
Run a Python script through uv without calling uv directly.

- Code never starts a registered program itself: it asks the tool registry (runToolV1), and repo verify tool-spawns refuses the spawns that bypass it.

units: repo units - Plan, run and emit language-neutral compilation units (Go, Python, .NET, C/C++, WIT, TeX) whose dependents re-run only when a dependency's interface changes, and execute one unit as the action of Nx or Bazel.
Usage:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel|semio] units plan|run|emit|exec [options]
Subcommands:
units plan --for=<language>                     Plan the units of the checkout and print their number, edges and layers (or the graph as JSON).
units run --for=<language> [--only=<unit>] [--concurrency=<n>] [--receipts=<dir>]
Run the units in dependency order; a unit whose key has a receipt is not run again.
units emit nx|bazel --for=<language> --out=<dir>
Write the spec files and the Nx targets or the Bazel rule and BUILD file of the units.
units exec --spec=<file> --out=<file> [--iface=<file>] [--iface-dep=<file>]... [--impl-dep=<file>]...
Execute one unit: the action of the generated Nx targets and Bazel rule.
Options:
--for=<names>         service issue: comma separated project names or prefixes ending in * the token is limited to.

--root=<path>         incremental, concurrency, bench: the disposable repository copy (default: the folder .sinc in the home directory, else sinc in the temporary directory of the process, else /tmp/sinc); it must not lie inside or contain the checkout, and its path stays short because absolute paths are limited to 256 characters.
--out=<path>          units emit: the directory that receives the spec files and the build files; units exec: the result file of the unit (out.json).
--out-root=<path>     units exec: read the files of the dependencies from and write the files of the unit below this directory (the layout the Nx targets use) instead of naming each file.
--spec=<path>         units exec: the spec file of the unit to execute.
--iface=<path>        units exec: the interface file (iface.json) the unit publishes.
--iface-dep=<path>    units exec: the interface file of one dependency whose interface the unit consumes; repeatable.
--impl-dep=<path>     units exec: a result file (out.json) of the implementation closure of the unit; repeatable.
--only=<area[,area]>  doctor: limit the report to these areas (tools, storage, leases, capacity, sessions, graph, dependencies, caches, processes, host).
--concurrency <n>     remote-execution serve|workers: actions one worker runs at the same time (default: one per CPU).
--receipts=<path>     units run: directory of the shared receipts, so later runs and other sessions reuse results (default: memory only).
--file=<path>         Write the result as a report file and print its path.
--json                Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line.

--tool=<nx|bazel|semio>       Select the build implementation; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, then the policy default (nx).

--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo units plan --for=go
Plan the Go units of the checkout.
repo units run --for=python --receipts=.units --concurrency=4
Run the Python units with shared receipts.
repo units emit bazel --for=python --out=.bazel-units
Write the Bazel rule and BUILD file of the Python units.
Notes:

- exec is the action both build tools run: it reads one unit spec and the published files of its dependencies, runs the language tool and writes out.json and iface.json. A failing unit exits non-zero.

- Bazel lists only the iface.json of interface dependencies, so an unchanged interface cuts off by itself. Go libraries compile directly against dependency export data, so Bazel cuts off at an unchanged export interface; binaries, tests, cgo packages and .NET projects read dependency sources (policy or unit marker bazel: sources) and rebuild with them; the cutoff then happens in units run.

bench: repo bench - Measure the performance objectives (hot-cache latency, edit to rebuild per language, cache hit rate, graph, memory, concurrent agents) in a disposable checkout copy, judge them against the SLO table and compare with a stored baseline; `bench acceptance` holds the acceptance scenarios of the three products (hot no-op, peer edit, one-line edit with byte-exact revert) on the checkout itself to declared budgets.
Usage:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel|semio] bench list|run|compare|acceptance [options]
Subcommands:
bench list                                      List the objectives with their probe, goal, gate and enforcement.
bench run [--slo=<ids|all>] [--runs=<n>] [--baseline=<report>] [--save-baseline=<report>] [--history=<folder>] [--prepare]
Measure the selected objectives with every implementation, print percentiles, host load and verdicts, and compare with the baseline.
bench compare --current=<report> --baseline=<report> | --history=<folder>
Compare two stored reports of the same host class, name every regression beyond the tolerance of its objective and every blocking objective over its budget.
bench acceptance [--scenario=<ids|all>] [--in-place]

Run the acceptance scenarios (hot no-op three times, peer edit, one-line edit with byte-exact revert) of the course, print and the dashboard through the official route on this checkout, with the exact wall clock and the physical footprint, judge them against the declared budgets and fail when a blocking budget is broken.
Options:
--slo=<ids|all>                     bench run: comma list of objective ids, probe:<id>, kind:<cli-help|noop|edit|graph|cache|concurrency>, or all.
--runs=<n>                          bench run: samples per probe instead of the authored count (the 95th percentile needs 20 samples, the 99th needs 100; fewer leave those objectives unproven).
--baseline=<path>                   bench run|compare: a stored report to compare with; a change beyond the tolerance of an objective is a regression or an improvement.
--save-baseline=<path>              bench run: store the report as the baseline of later runs.
--current=<path>                    bench compare: the stored report to judge against --baseline.

--history=<folder>                  bench run: store the report in this folder as <UTC start>-<host class>.json and compare with the newest earlier report of this host class when no --baseline is given; bench compare: compare the two newest reports of this host class.
--markdown=<path>                   bench run|compare|acceptance: also write the report as a markdown file.
--max-load=<per-core>               bench run: refuse to start when the one-minute load per core of the host exceeds this number.
--prepare                           bench run: discard and prepare the disposable copy first, so that the cold graph probe starts from a copy without graph.
--implementations=<nx|bazel|semio>  incremental and concurrency plan|run: implementations to judge (default: every registered backend).

--root=<path>                       incremental, concurrency, bench: the disposable repository copy (default: the folder .sinc in the home directory, else sinc in the temporary directory of the process, else /tmp/sinc); it must not lie inside or contain the checkout, and its path stays short because absolute paths are limited to 256 characters.
--file=<path>                       Write the result as a report file and print its path.
--json                              Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line.

--scenario=<ids|all>                incremental plan|run and bench acceptance: comma list of scenario ids, or all (bench acceptance also takes kind:<noop|peer|edit> and product:<course|print|dashboard>; without --in-place, all leaves the scenarios that edit files out).
--in-place                          bench acceptance: run the scenarios that edit and restore source files in this checkout (a CI runner, a private clone); nobody else may edit it meanwhile.

--workers=<on|off>            Run actions in persistent workers (on) or in one process each (off); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, then the worker policy of the build policy.
--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo bench list
List the performance objectives.
repo bench run --slo=kind:noop --baseline=bench-baseline.json
Measure the warm no-op objectives and compare with the stored baseline.
repo bench acceptance --in-place --file=acceptance.json --markdown=acceptance.md
Run every acceptance scenario on this checkout and fail when a blocking budget is broken.

Print the cache ledger without walking any tree (statfs of each partition plus the recorded sizes; --deep walks everything): every partition and area with its use against its budget, the retired roots and undeclared entries still on disk; with --tasks, a CacheStatus of the selected tool instead.
cache gc [--dry-run] [--area=<id>] [--budget=<size>]

Collect the cache: remove retired roots, units unused longer than their area allows and the oldest units beyond an area's budget, and entries nobody declared; it never removes a unit that is held by a lease or used recently.

cache verify --deep [--json]                    Read every indexed optional graph leaf and every content-addressed closure inventory again, compare each with its recorded hash or name and print what differs; the only command that re-reads leaf bytes after they were written.

cache dedupe [--dry-run] [--area=<id>]          Find identical large files inside the declared places of the machine budget (Bazel outputs and workspaces, Vite products, tool installs) and replace each duplicate by a copy-on-write clone of one canonical file, freeing the duplicated blocks; files used recently, with volatile names or changed meanwhile are kept, a volume that cannot clone keeps everything, and --dry-run only reports what would be freed at most.
cache clear                                     Empty the cache and print a CacheClear.
Options:
--json            Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line.
--dry-run         Print the task graph as a DryRunPlan on stdout and execute nothing; the same for every tool. With cache gc or remote-cache gc: list what would be removed and remove nothing.

--area=<id[,id]>  cache status|gc: limit the report or the collection to these ledger areas (or retired, undeclared); cache dedupe: limit the search to these places (bazel-outputs, bazel-workspaces, vite-products, tools).

--budget=<size>   cache status|gc: the disk budget of this machine for this call (an integer or a number with KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, e.g. 40GiB); it beats the SEMIO_CACHE_BUDGET_BYTES variable, which beats the machine file in the repository cache root, which beats the declared default.

--deep            cache verify (required): read every indexed optional graph leaf and every closure inventory again and compare it with its recorded hash. cache status: walk every cache home now (with progress, cancellable) and record the sizes, instead of reading statfs and the size ledger.
--tasks           cache status: print the selected tool's task cache (a CacheStatus) instead of the cache ledger.
Global options:
--tool=<nx|bazel|semio>       Select the build implementation; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, then the policy default (nx).
--workers=<on|off>            Run actions in persistent workers (on) or in one process each (off); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, then the worker policy of the build policy.
--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo cache status
Show every cache partition and area against its budget.
repo cache gc --dry-run
List what the collector would remove.
repo cache gc --dry-run --budget=40GiB
Plan the collection against a 40 GiB machine budget.
repo cache dedupe --dry-run
Report how many bytes identical files waste in the declared places.
repo cache verify --deep
Re-read and re-hash every indexed optional graph leaf and closure inventory.
repo cache status --tasks --tool=bazel
Show the Bazel disk cache and build activity.
repo cache clear
Empty the Nx task cache.
Notes:

- status prints the cache ledger of schema cache-ledger: every fixed partition, every area inside a partition, every area of the repository and native cache roots with its declared budget, and what is retired or undeclared; gc collects it. Both publish progress, stop at the next checkpoint when the caller cancels, and take no lease for the report, which reads statfs of each partition and the size ledger that gc and --deep write and walks no tree unless --deep is given; gc takes an area's lease exclusively without waiting and never removes a unit whose SQLite lease file is locked, whose queue ticket belongs to a living process or that was used within the quiet time of its area. Areas kept by an owner (Nx at maxCacheSize, Cargo, Bazel, test evidence, the dashboard) are reported, not collected here.

- One machine disk budget governs every cache (schema machine-disk-budget): a total in bytes, 40 GiB by default and set per machine with --budget, the SEMIO_CACHE_BUDGET_BYTES variable or the file in the repository cache root, is shared out to the stores (the image partitions and everything loose) by weight with floors and a headroom per image. Stores are filled by weighted max-min fairness over what they hold, so a store below its fair share is never cut. status prints each store's quota, what must go and the image size that would fit; gc enforces the loose store's quota least recently used first, never touching a unit a live process holds or that was used recently, and leaves the images to their owners, whose free-space thresholds act once the images are recreated at the planned size.

- Optional graph caches are retired by an append-only member index per group (name, size, kind, stamp and the sha256 of every leaf, taken once when the leaf is written; the shared namespace and the generation documents keep one too) plus an lstat of each member, never by reading leaf bytes; gc indexes a group the index cannot vouch for before it may be retired, holding that group's non-blocking writer lease only while it appends rows, never while it reads leaves. verify --deep reads and hashes every indexed leaf and every closure inventory again and prints what differs, publishes progress and stops at the next checkpoint when the caller cancels.
- status --tasks prints a CacheStatus, clear prints a CacheClear; both stop at the next checkpoint when the caller cancels and publish progress while walking or removing entries.
- Nx: status walks the artifacts directory of the Nx cache partition, clear resets only the Nx task cache inside the bounded Nx namespace.

- Bazel: status counts the files of the disk cache entry folders (action cache and content-addressed store) of the products partition and adds the recorded build activity (builds, actions, executed, cacheHits) read from the build event stream; clear stops the persistent servers, removes their output bases (the local action cache) and empties the disk cache, so the next build is a miss; toolchains and modules stay.

remote-cache: repo remote-cache - Serve a bounded, shared result cache for Bazel and Nx from this machine, inspect the remote cache contract and the server, or collect the cache store.
Usage:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel|semio] remote-cache serve|status|gc [options]
Subcommands:
remote-cache serve [--port <n>] [--host <address>] [--directory <path>] [--max-bytes <n>] [--read-only] [--tls-certificate <path> --tls-key <path>]
Serve the store over HTTP (or HTTPS) until stopped: Bazel's HTTP cache protocol and the Nx self-hosted cache API share one content-addressed, bounded store.

remote-cache status [--directory <path>]        Print a RemoteCacheStatus: the remote cache contract, how Nx and Bazel render it, one read-only probe per protocol, what the running server reports and what the local store holds.
remote-cache gc [--dry-run] [--json] [--directory <path>] [--max-bytes <n>]
Collect the store from outside, also while a server runs: remove unusable action results, entries idle for too long and the least recently used entries beyond the bound; --dry-run only plans.
Options:
--port <port>             remote-cache serve: port to listen on; 0 picks a free port (default from the build policy).
--host <address>          remote-cache serve: address to listen on; beyond loopback a token is required.
--directory <path>        remote-cache serve|status|gc: store directory, relative to the workspace root (default: the remote cache home of the cache ledger).
--max-bytes <bytes>       remote-cache serve|gc: upper bound of the store; the least recently used entries are evicted beyond it.
--read-only               remote-cache serve: refuse every write with 403, whatever token is presented.
--tls-certificate <path>  remote-cache serve, remote-execution serve: PEM certificate chain; together with --tls-key the server speaks HTTPS (grpcs for the execution service).
--tls-key <path>          remote-cache serve, remote-execution serve: PEM private key of the certificate.
--json                    Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line.
--dry-run                 Print the task graph as a DryRunPlan on stdout and execute nothing; the same for every tool. With cache gc or remote-cache gc: list what would be removed and remove nothing.

capacity: repo capacity - Show the machine's free memory, floor, load and the running and waiting grants, or run any command under a machine-wide capacity grant.
Usage:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel|semio] capacity status|run [options]
Subcommands:
capacity status [--json]                        Print the host sample, the free-memory floor, every running grant with what it reserved and what it holds, and every waiting request.
capacity run [--operation=<name>|--memory=<megabytes> [--cpu=<cores>]] [--jobs=<n>] -- <command> <args>
Wait in the machine-wide queue until the host can carry the command, run it with the grant in its environment and give the grant back when it ends.
Options:
--json                Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line.
--operation=<name>    capacity run: the catalogue operation whose estimate is reserved (default: command).
--memory=<megabytes>  capacity run: reserve exactly this many megabytes instead of an operation's estimate.
--cpu=<cores>         capacity run: cores the command keeps busy, counted against the load ceiling (default: 1).
--jobs=<n>            capacity run: jobs of a task operation to reserve (default: 1).
Global options:
--tool=<nx|bazel|semio>       Select the build implementation; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, then the policy default (nx).
--workers=<on|off>            Run actions in persistent workers (on) or in one process each (off); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, then the worker policy of the build policy.
--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo capacity status
See how much memory the machine has left above its floor and who holds it.
repo capacity run --memory=6144 -- repo tools exec bun -- test ./some.test.ts
Run an ad-hoc test runner only when 6 GB can be reserved.
repo capacity run --operation=dependencies -- repo dependencies sync --all
Reserve what a dependency sync is estimated to need.
Notes:
- Every heavy repo command (run, run-many, affected, exec, watch, cargo, show, graph, dependencies) is admitted the same way before it starts; capacity run does it for everything else.

- A request is admitted while the free memory stays above the floor (a share of the host memory between 4 and 8 GB), the swap stays below its ceiling and the load below its ceiling per core, the machine-wide open file table stays below its ceiling share and fewer disk images are attached than the maximum (the last three are waited out and overridden only when nothing of ours runs); memory pressure at the critical level admits nobody. Requests are served first come first served, interactive before batch.

- The grant sets the parallelism of the selected tool through that tool's own limits: the task parallelism for Nx, the job and local-resource limits for Bazel, the core count for Cargo. SEMIO_HOST_CAPACITY=off switches the governor off explicitly.
- Waiting prints a progress line in the chosen language and stops at the next checkpoint when the caller cancels; the grant of a process that dies is reclaimed automatically.

leases: repo leases - Show which processes hold and wait for resource leases, how long, who blocks whom, deadlock cycles, lock order violations and the machine's admission queue.
Usage:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel|semio] leases status [options]
Subcommands:
leases status [--json] [--all] [--lease-directory=<path>] [--violations=<n>]
Print every held and awaited lease with mode, class, holder, hold duration, queue position and blockers, the wait-for graph, deadlock cycles, recent order violations and the admission queue.
Options:
--json                    Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line.
--all                     Select every project (affected, watch), every dependency owner (dependencies) or every lease directory with registered processes (leases).
--lease-directory=<path>  leases status: the lease directory to inspect (default: the checkout's lease store).
--violations=<n>          leases status: how many recent lock order violations to list (default: 10).
Global options:
--tool=<nx|bazel|semio>       Select the build implementation; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, then the policy default (nx).
--workers=<on|off>            Run actions in persistent workers (on) or in one process each (off); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, then the worker policy of the build policy.
--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo leases status
See who holds the repository's leases, who waits behind whom and for how long.
repo leases status --all --json
Machine-readable state of every lease directory that registered a process.
Notes:

- Leases are declared in lock classes with a rank (SEMIO_LEASE_ORDER=off|observe|enforce overrides the declared rules). A request that breaks the order, closes a deadlock cycle, or waits beyond the grace period while its task holds another lease exclusively fails fast with a diagnostic naming the blocking process.
- Processes register what they hold and await in the per-user lease registry (SEMIO_LEASE_REGISTRY_DIRECTORY overrides its location); entries of dead processes are ignored and removed.

Run the shared store (unless one is named), the scheduler with its gRPC listener for build tools and its HTTP listener for workers, and local worker processes, until stopped; prints the variables a client sets and the command another machine joins with.

remote-execution status [--join <url>]          Print a RemoteExecutionStatus: the client contract, whether the gRPC endpoint answers the protocol's capabilities call, and what the scheduler reports (workers, queues, counters).
remote-execution workers --join <url> [--name <name>] [--concurrency <n>] [--sandbox <strategy>] [--properties <name=value,...>] [--work-directory <path>]
Run a worker of this machine (or devcontainer) that joins a scheduler, runs the hermetic actions it is handed in a sandbox and reports until stopped.
Options:
--bind <address>                                remote-execution serve: address both listeners bind to (default 127.0.0.1); beyond loopback the cache tokens and the worker token are required.
--grpc-port <port>                              remote-execution serve: port of the gRPC listener for build tools (default 8980); 0 picks a free port.
--worker-port <port>                            remote-execution serve: port of the HTTP listener for workers and status (default 8981); 0 picks a free port.
--cache <url>                                   remote-execution serve: the shared store to use, the URL of a running repo remote-cache server; by default serve starts the store itself.
--local-workers <n>                             remote-execution serve: worker processes started with the service (default 1; 0 starts none).
--concurrency <n>                               remote-execution serve|workers: actions one worker runs at the same time (default: one per CPU).
--advertise <host>                              remote-execution serve: the host name clients and workers use to reach the service (default: loopback, else this machine's name).
--sandbox <auto|darwin-sandbox|linux-sandbox|isolated-root>
remote-execution serve|workers: how workers confine an action (default: the first available strategy of the hermetic table for this host).

--work-directory <path>                         remote-execution serve|workers: directory of a worker's blob cache and private input roots, relative to the workspace root (default: the remote execution home of the cache ledger).
--join <url>                                    remote-execution workers|status: the worker API of the scheduler, for example http://build-host:8981 (default: SEMIO_REMOTE_EXECUTION_SCHEDULER).
--name <name>                                   remote-execution workers: name of the worker in status and logs (default: host name and process id).
--properties <name=value,...>                   remote-execution workers: platform properties the worker offers in addition to OSFamily and Arch.
--tls-certificate <path>                        remote-cache serve, remote-execution serve: PEM certificate chain; together with --tls-key the server speaks HTTPS (grpcs for the execution service).
--tls-key <path>                                remote-cache serve, remote-execution serve: PEM private key of the certificate.
Global options:
--tool=<nx|bazel|semio>       Select the build implementation; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, then the policy default (nx).
--workers=<on|off>            Run actions in persistent workers (on) or in one process each (off); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, then the worker policy of the build policy.
--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo remote-execution serve
Run the service on 127.0.0.1:8980 with the shared store and one local worker; hermetic Bazel actions can then run remotely.
repo remote-execution workers --join http://build-host:8981
Add this machine as a worker of a service that runs elsewhere.
repo remote-execution status
Show the client contract, whether the endpoint answers and which workers are registered.
Notes:

- Remote execution is off for clients until SEMIO_REMOTE_EXECUTION_ENDPOINT names a grpc or grpcs origin; while it is unset every action stays local. SEMIO_REMOTE_EXECUTION_PLATFORM (default linux-x64), _INSTANCE (default main), _PROPERTIES and _JOBS are read by the Bazel implementation; serve prints the endpoint, platform and instance of this machine. Only hermetic actions are sent, with no local fallback: an unreachable service fails the build.

- The service implements the subset of the Remote Execution API v2 that Bazel needs, over gRPC on HTTP/2 with the repository's own wire codec: capabilities, execution (also waiting for an operation), action cache, content-addressable storage and ByteStream. Bazel offloads execution only over this protocol, and refuses an HTTP cache beside a gRPC executor, so the service is the cache too: it keeps its blobs and results in the shared store of repo remote-cache (started inside serve, or named with --cache), and the Bazel implementation drops its HTTP cache flags while an executor is configured. Identical actions in flight run once; results of successful actions enter the action cache.

- Workers pull work: each long-polls the scheduler's HTTP listener (default port 8981), offers its platform properties (OSFamily and Arch of its machine, plus --properties) and runs the actions whose required properties it offers, up to --concurrency at once. Every action gets a private input root built from the store, exactly its declared environment, and the sandbox of the hermetic table for the host: darwin-sandbox on macOS (no network, writes only inside the root), linux-sandbox (bubblewrap) on Linux, otherwise isolated-root, the private root alone (always the case on Windows); --sandbox pins one. A worker that stops heartbeating loses its work to another worker; cancelling a call or a timeout kills the whole process tree. --local-workers sets how many worker processes serve starts (default 1, 0 starts none).

- Tokens: the read and write tokens of repo remote-cache (SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_SERVER_READ_TOKEN, SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_SERVER_WRITE_TOKEN) also guard the gRPC listener (read: lookups and downloads; write: everything including execution), and SEMIO_REMOTE_EXECUTION_WORKER_TOKEN guards the worker API; beyond loopback --bind refuses to start without them. Workers read the cache token from SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_TOKEN. --tls-certificate and --tls-key switch both listeners to TLS (grpcs). serve, workers and status publish progress and stop at the next checkpoint when the caller cancels; the output follows SEMIO_LANGUAGE or --lang and is printed in both languages when neither is set.

Options:
--bind <address>                                remote-execution serve: address both listeners bind to (default 127.0.0.1); beyond loopback the cache tokens and the worker token are required.
--grpc-port <port>                              remote-execution serve: port of the gRPC listener for build tools (default 8980); 0 picks a free port.
--worker-port <port>                            remote-execution serve: port of the HTTP listener for workers and status (default 8981); 0 picks a free port.
--cache <url>                                   remote-execution serve: the shared store to use, the URL of a running repo remote-cache server; by default serve starts the store itself.
--local-workers <n>                             remote-execution serve: worker processes started with the service (default 1; 0 starts none).
--concurrency <n>                               remote-execution serve|workers: actions one worker runs at the same time (default: one per CPU).
--advertise <host>                              remote-execution serve: the host name clients and workers use to reach the service (default: loopback, else this machine's name).
--sandbox <auto|darwin-sandbox|linux-sandbox|isolated-root>
remote-execution serve|workers: how workers confine an action (default: the first available strategy of the hermetic table for this host).

--work-directory <path>                         remote-execution serve|workers: directory of a worker's blob cache and private input roots, relative to the workspace root (default: the remote execution home of the cache ledger).
--tls-certificate <path>                        remote-cache serve, remote-execution serve: PEM certificate chain; together with --tls-key the server speaks HTTPS (grpcs for the execution service).
--tls-key <path>                                remote-cache serve, remote-execution serve: PEM private key of the certificate.
Global options:
--tool=<nx|bazel|semio>       Select the build implementation; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, then the policy default (nx).
--workers=<on|off>            Run actions in persistent workers (on) or in one process each (off); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, then the worker policy of the build policy.
--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo remote-execution serve
Run the service on 127.0.0.1:8980 with the shared store and one local worker; hermetic Bazel actions can then run remotely.
Notes:

- Remote execution is off for clients until SEMIO_REMOTE_EXECUTION_ENDPOINT names a grpc or grpcs origin; while it is unset every action stays local. SEMIO_REMOTE_EXECUTION_PLATFORM (default linux-x64), _INSTANCE (default main), _PROPERTIES and _JOBS are read by the Bazel implementation; serve prints the endpoint, platform and instance of this machine. Only hermetic actions are sent, with no local fallback: an unreachable service fails the build.

- The service implements the subset of the Remote Execution API v2 that Bazel needs, over gRPC on HTTP/2 with the repository's own wire codec: capabilities, execution (also waiting for an operation), action cache, content-addressable storage and ByteStream. Bazel offloads execution only over this protocol, and refuses an HTTP cache beside a gRPC executor, so the service is the cache too: it keeps its blobs and results in the shared store of repo remote-cache (started inside serve, or named with --cache), and the Bazel implementation drops its HTTP cache flags while an executor is configured. Identical actions in flight run once; results of successful actions enter the action cache.

- Workers pull work: each long-polls the scheduler's HTTP listener (default port 8981), offers its platform properties (OSFamily and Arch of its machine, plus --properties) and runs the actions whose required properties it offers, up to --concurrency at once. Every action gets a private input root built from the store, exactly its declared environment, and the sandbox of the hermetic table for the host: darwin-sandbox on macOS (no network, writes only inside the root), linux-sandbox (bubblewrap) on Linux, otherwise isolated-root, the private root alone (always the case on Windows); --sandbox pins one. A worker that stops heartbeating loses its work to another worker; cancelling a call or a timeout kills the whole process tree. --local-workers sets how many worker processes serve starts (default 1, 0 starts none).

- Tokens: the read and write tokens of repo remote-cache (SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_SERVER_READ_TOKEN, SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_SERVER_WRITE_TOKEN) also guard the gRPC listener (read: lookups and downloads; write: everything including execution), and SEMIO_REMOTE_EXECUTION_WORKER_TOKEN guards the worker API; beyond loopback --bind refuses to start without them. Workers read the cache token from SEMIO_REMOTE_CACHE_TOKEN. --tls-certificate and --tls-key switch both listeners to TLS (grpcs). serve, workers and status publish progress and stop at the next checkpoint when the caller cancels; the output follows SEMIO_LANGUAGE or --lang and is printed in both languages when neither is set.

doctor: repo doctor - Answer in one shot why work is waiting, slow or failing: tool pins, storage images, leases, capacity grants, agent sessions, graph and dependency generations, caches, running repo processes and the host, each problem with its owner and the command that resolves it.
Usage:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel|semio] doctor [--json] [--fix [--dry-run]] [--only=<area>[,<area>]] [--strict] [--facts] [options]
Options:
--json                Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line.

--fix                 doctor: apply the declared safe repairs for the findings (publications of dead processes, stale lease registry rows, gone agent sessions); with --dry-run list what they would remove.
--dry-run             Print the task graph as a DryRunPlan on stdout and execute nothing; the same for every tool. With cache gc or remote-cache gc: list what would be removed and remove nothing.
--only=<area[,area]>  doctor: limit the report to these areas (tools, storage, leases, capacity, sessions, graph, dependencies, caches, processes, host).
--strict              doctor: exit with status 1 for warnings as well as errors.
--facts               doctor: print the raw facts document the findings are derived from, as JSON, instead of the report.
Global options:
--tool=<nx|bazel|semio>       Select the build implementation; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, then the policy default (nx).
--workers=<on|off>            Run actions in persistent workers (on) or in one process each (off); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, then the worker policy of the build policy.
--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo doctor
See who waits for whom, what is slow and what is broken, with the command that fixes each finding.
repo doctor --only=leases,capacity
Look only at leases, capacity and the processes behind them.
repo doctor --fix --dry-run
List what the safe repairs would remove.
repo doctor --fix
Remove dead-process publications, stale lease registry rows and gone agent sessions, then read the state again.
repo doctor --json
The report as JSON for tools and agents.
Notes:
- doctor reads state only: it takes no lease and no capacity grant, so it answers even while a build holds everything, and it never starts a heavy command.
- Areas: tools, storage, leases, capacity, sessions, graph, dependencies, caches, processes, host. Exit status 1 when an error remains (a warning too with --strict), 130 when cancelled.
- --fix applies only repairs that are declared safe in the doctor policy; every other finding names the command to run or whom to ask.
session: repo session - Show, open and close agent sessions: one identity per agent working in this worktree, with its cargo lane, Bazel slot preference, Nx daemon namespace, test sandbox root, lease owner tag, budget share and capability.
Usage:
repo [--tool=nx|bazel|semio] session open|status|close|list [options]
Subcommands:
session open [--agent=<name>] [--client=<name>] [--client-pid=<pid>] [--owner-pid=<pid>] [--weight=<n>] [--export] [--json]

Open the session of the calling agent, or attach to it when it exists. The agent is named by --agent, else by the client's own session variable, else by the connection (--client), else by the nearest agent-client ancestor process, else the default session.

session status [<id>] [--json]                  Print one session (default: the current one): identity, state, owner process, every derived resource name, budget share, capability and what it holds right now (leases, capacity grants, test sandboxes).
session close <id> [--force] [--json] | session close --dead [--json]
Close a session and release its test sandboxes and temp root, or close every gone session. A live session is refused unless --force is given.
session list [--all] [--json]                   List the sessions of this worktree (every worktree with --all) with agent, client, state, budget share and last use.
Options:
--json              Print lists as JSON instead of one entry per line.
--all               Select every project (affected, watch), every dependency owner (dependencies) or every lease directory with registered processes (leases).
--agent=<id>        service issue: the agent the token is issued to; service revoke: revoke every session of this agent.
--client=<name>     session open: the name of the agent client, used to name the agent of an MCP connection when no client variable identifies it.
--client-pid=<pid>  session open: the process id of the agent client of a connection (part of the connection's identity).
--owner-pid=<pid>   session open: a process whose end ends the session (default: the nearest agent-client ancestor).
--weight=<n>        session open: the weight of the session in the budget split between live sessions, 1 to 16 (default: 1).
--export            session open: also print the environment line NAME=value that attaches child processes to the session.
--dead              session close: close every gone session instead of one.
--force             session close: close a session although its owner process is still alive.
Global options:
--tool=<nx|bazel|semio>       Select the build implementation; otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_TOOL, then the policy default (nx).
--workers=<on|off>            Run actions in persistent workers (on) or in one process each (off); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_WORKERS, then the worker policy of the build policy.
--service=<auto|off|require>  Use the resident service (auto: when one answers), never use it (off), or fail when none answers (require); otherwise SEMIO_BUILD_SERVICE, then auto.
-h, --help                    Print the usage of the command and stop.

--lang=<en|de>                Language of the texts; otherwise SEMIO_LANGUAGE, then LANGUAGE and the locale variables (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG), then the operating system language. No language is assumed: the command refuses when none resolves.
Examples:
repo session status
See which agent session this command belongs to and what it holds.
repo session list --all --json
Machine-readable list of every agent session of every worktree on this host.
repo session close --dead
Release the sandboxes and temp roots of every session whose process tree is gone.
Notes:

- Every repo command attaches to its session at the door and passes only its address (SEMIO_AGENT_SESSION) to child processes; every tool adapter reads the session from that one API. Sessions of a gone process tree are collected automatically at most once a minute.
- The budget share of a session is its weight divided by the weights of all live sessions; the machine admission queue serves the session with the least reserved memory per weight first.
